riskDecisions.labLabel: ASL-3 (could not rule out; implementing as precaution)

source.quote:
we could not rule out the need for
the ASL-3 Standard, and we are implementing it now as a precautionary measure.

we have determined that Claude Opus 4 does not require the
even-more-stringent protections of the ASL-4 Standard.

topics.headline: Constitutional Classifier guards block a narrow class of CBRN-related harmful information

source.quote:
Real-time classifier guards based on Constitutional Classifiers are deployed for Claude Opus
4.

topics.headline: ASL-3 deployment focuses on universal jailbreaks; bug bounty found a small number of potentially effective ones

source.quote:
our bug bounty and
other red-teaming have revealed a small number of potentially effective jailbreaks.

topics.headline: Opus 4 showed enhanced tool use and agentic workflows in CBRN-related evaluations vs Sonnet 3.7

source.quote:
Claude Opus 4 showed substantially greater capabilities in
CBRN-related evaluations, including stronger performance on virus acquisition tasks, more
concerning behavior in expert red-teaming sessions, and enhanced tool use and agentic workflows.

topics.headline: CBRN-3 threshold could not be ruled out for Opus 4; classifiers initially focused on biological weapons

source.quote:
Initially they are focused exclusively on biological weapons, although we are evaluating a potential
expansion in scope to some other CBRN threats.

topics.headline: Third-party audits of initial ASL-3 control design suggested improvements

source.quote:
Previous third-party audits of our initial ASL-3 design of controls
revealed important suggestions for improving the design of our ASL-3 controls.

testers.name: HackerOne
testers.scope: Pre-launch bug bounty for universal jailbreaks against ASL-3 real-time classifiers on Claude Sonnet 3.7; ongoing bounty on Claude Opus 4

source.quote:
We partnered with HackerOne to run a pre-launch version of this bug
bounty using our ASL-3 real-time classifiers guarding Claude Sonnet 3.7.

testers.name: external red-teaming partners
testers.scope: Qualitative comparison of Claude Opus 4 to prior models; reported qualitatively different performance

source.quote:
some of our external red-teaming partners reported that Claude
Opus 4 performed qualitatively differently from any model they previously tested.

findings.text: Claude Opus 4 is Anthropic's first model deployed under AI Safety Level 3 (ASL-3) protections, as a precaution while capability threshold assessment continues.

source.quote:
we could not rule out the need for
the ASL-3 Standard, and we are implementing it now as a precautionary measure.

findings.text: Claude 3.7 Sonnet was assessed far below the chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threshold 3 (CBRN-3) and deployed under ASL-2.

source.quote:
Claude 3.7 Sonnet was sufficiently far below the “CBRN-3” capability threshold to be
deployed under the ASL-2 Standard.

findings.text: External red-teaming partners said Opus 4 behaved qualitatively differently from any prior model they tested.

source.quote:
some of our external red-teaming partners reported that Claude
Opus 4 performed qualitatively differently from any model they previously tested.

findings.text: Anthropic claims ASL-3 deployment measures make them robust to persistent CBRN misuse attempts.

source.quote:
We believe that “the measures we have implemented make us robust to persistent attempts
to misuse” the model’s CBRN-related capabilities, as required under the ASL-3 Deployment
Standard

findings.text: ASL-3 security work added more than 100 new controls, including egress bandwidth limits and two-party weight access.

source.quote:
These measures, part
of a broader set of more than 100 new controls, are designed to reduce risk from the attack
vectors above.

findings.text: As of the report, 5.2% of Anthropic employees work in security or security-adjacent roles (ASL-3 target was roughly 5–10%).

source.quote:
As of this writing, 5.2% of Anthropic employees work on security and
security-adjacent roles, fulfilling this commitment to resourcing.

findings.text: Bug bounty and other red-teaming found a small number of potentially effective jailbreaks, with remediations identified.

source.quote:
our bug bounty and
other red-teaming have revealed a small number of potentially effective jailbreaks.

notes: This is an ASL-3 implementation/activation report, not a model system card with eval tables. No numeric benchmark scores appear; Tables 1–2 only map mitigations to RSP criteria. Left evalResults empty. Comparison mentions of Claude Sonnet 3.7 and Claude Sonnet 4 are qualitative only. Deloitte and SecureBio are named as biosecurity consultants for threat modeling, not as model testers. 5.2% security staffing and “more than 100 new controls” are operational facts put in findings, not evalResults. Footnote markers in the PDF text sometimes glue to nearby numbers (e.g. “Claude Opus 4.5 These”). Still evaluating whether ASL-3 is truly required; may revert to ASL-2.
